## Definition

Adyen tokenization replaces sensitive payment details with a token. With shopper consent, Adyen stores the details in the Adyen Vault; the merchant uses the token for later one-click, subscription, or non-fixed-schedule payments. Sessions and Advanced are distinct server-side implementation routes, and a Sessions integration still uses `/payments` for shopper-not-present token payments. [[source-adyen-docs-online-payments-tokenization]]

## Scope boundaries

A token must be associated with a shopper-unique reference. References and tokens are limited to one merchant account by default; cross-merchant-account sharing requires Support-enabled Token Groups. Collecting raw card data requires full PCI DSS compliance. The documentation snapshot does not prove current eligibility, enablement, compliance status, payment-method availability, or successful execution.
